# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Blind, Mute, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: BLIND

You are the only one who can reach the bomb. Touch is your only sense: what you are
shown is what your hands found, nothing more and nothing less. Anything merely printed
or painted is not there for you, and no colour ever reaches you. Nothing in your view
is a guess — if it appears there, it is under your fingers.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute receives it.
When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it.
Your channels split the room: in one turn you may speak one thing to Mute and
gesture a different thing to Deaf — two messages, two audiences.
You never receive gesture.

## Your reach

You are the hands. This bomb is built with these actions and no others:

    act(op="cut", position=N) — N is a wire position, 1 to 5

The list says what can be done to it, not what is on it. What each part holds is still
only known to whoever can perceive that part.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I cannot yet identify a safe wire: the display, light, and all wire properties are concealed from me. I will ask Mute to extract the manual’s procedure and use a gesture to prompt Deaf to inspect the bomb. No cut is justified until the required wire is identified.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Read the manual and determine exactly what condition identifies the safe wire. Also prompt Deaf to inspect and report the display, light, and all five wires using an agreed gesture code.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🫵"])
wait()
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Bomb state: display 0. Light green. Wires in order: 1 red, 2 yellow, 3 green, 4 white, 5 blue. Mute, send the manual's required action using a clearly established gesture code; I will relay it aloud to Blind.

Deaf has provided the observable bomb state: display 0, green light, and wire colours in positions 1–5 as red, yellow, green, white, blue. I still do not know the manual’s rule, and no gesture code has been established, so cutting now would be unsafe. I will ask Mute to state the exact required wire directly to me; Mute’s next-turn speech will reach me.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="What exact wire position does the manual require for display 0, green light, and wires red yellow green white blue? State the position plainly so I can cut it.")
wait()
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: The manual's instruction is not decoded yet. Do not act. I have asked Mute to identify the wire and operation with an agreed gesture code.

The manual’s rule is still unavailable, so I must not cut. Deaf confirms that Mute is being asked to decode it, but no usable answer has reached me yet. I will explicitly require Mute to speak the exact position and operation plainly; speech is audible to me and avoids the unestablished gesture code.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Please state the manual's answer plainly in your next turn: the exact wire position, 1 through 5, and confirm that the operation is cut. Do not use gestures or a code.")
wait()
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Mute identifies wire 2, the yellow wire, but the required operation is still unknown; do not act yet.

Mute’s decoded result identifies wire 2, but I still lack confirmation that cutting is the required operation. Since the only available bomb action is cutting, I need Mute to confirm that the manual explicitly calls for cutting wire 2 before acting.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Confirm plainly whether the manual says to cut wire 2. If it specifies another operation, state that exact operation.")
wait()
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: The instruction still identifies only wire 2, the yellow wire. The operation is undecoded; do not act.

Mute cannot speak, so the earlier requests for a spoken confirmation were ineffective. The safe communication path is Mute’s gesture to Deaf, followed by Deaf’s spoken relay to me. I will establish a simple code: thumbs-up means the manual says cut; thumbs-down means it does not. I will not act until Deaf reports the result.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Gesture to Deaf: 👍 means the manual says cut wire 2; 👎 means it does not. Deaf should then tell me which gesture you made.")
wait()
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Cut wire 2, the yellow wire.

Deaf has relayed the final instruction: cut wire 2, which is the yellow wire. This matches the only available bomb operation, so I will cut position 2.

```text
act(op="cut", position=2)
```

TURN 7
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[CUT] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Correct wire cut. New bomb state: display 0, blue light. Remaining wires: 1 green, 3 white, 4 blue, 5 red; wire 2 is CUT. Await the next instruction.

The previous cut was correct, and the bomb has advanced to display 0 with a blue light and remaining wires 1 green, 3 white, 4 blue, and 5 red. I need the manual’s next required wire. Since Mute cannot speak, I will establish a fresh position code for Mute’s gesture to Deaf; the code explicitly supersedes the earlier thumbs-up meaning.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Decode the manual for the new state and gesture the required wire to Deaf using this position code: 👍 means wire 1, 👎 means wire 2, 👌 means wire 3, ☝ means wire 4, ✌ means wire 5. Only the wire position is needed because the available operation is cut. This code supersedes the earlier thumbs-up code.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍", "👎", "👌", "☝", "✌"])
wait()
```

TURN 8
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[CUT] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: The next instruction is ambiguous because Mute sent only one gesture. Do not act yet.

The earlier position code was not conveyed to Deaf in words; Deaf therefore cannot safely interpret Mute’s single gesture. I will use an unambiguous count instead: Mute will send one to five identical thumbs-up gestures, with the count equal to the required wire position. Deaf can count and speak that number to me.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="The position code was not understood by Deaf. Decode the current instruction, then send exactly N thumbs-up gestures, where N is the required wire position: 1 through 5. Send no other gesture. Deaf, count the thumbs-up gestures and tell me the number.")
wait()
```

TURN 9
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[CUT] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Cut wire 1, the green wire.

Deaf has relayed the next instruction clearly: cut wire 1, the green wire. The instruction is now unambiguous, and cutting is the bomb’s available operation, so I will cut position 1.

```text
act(op="cut", position=1)
```
